findings.issue: `_dataset_of` caches the instantiated dataset under `OmegaConf.to_yaml(cfg.dataset)`, which is the UNRESOLVED subtree (`seed: ${data_seed}`, `n_train: ${n_data}`) and is therefore byte-identical for every data seed / n_data of a scan. The first dataset built in a process is then reused for every other run. Demonstrated on the real results: in one process, `load_run('toy_1d_scan_confirm', ...data_seed1000...)` then data_seed1001 and 1002 return the SAME object (id identical, `ds.split_seed=1000` while the record says 1001/1002, `train[0]=(-0.584906,-0.207050)` for all three), whereas an independent `instantiate` of each config gives (-0.584906,-0.207050) / (0.543525,0.329180) / (0.362286,1.345471). A sweep over all 21 scans hit 8/12 sampled runs in `toy_1d_scan_confirm` and 8/12 in `polynomial_scan_confirm` (silent: probe_set/batch_of_step/checkpoint_spectra would use the wrong data; verify_checkpoint would just look 'failed'), and all three `rebuttal_overparam_*` scans raise (`rebuilt dataset has 1200 training examples but the record says 150`) because there the n_train guard catches it. The delivered diag caches are unaffected (single data seed) - I reproduced every cached number exactly - but the confirm passes with 3 data seeds are exactly what ANALYSIS_PLAN section 2.1 / F27 asks phase B to analyse.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the cache on the RESOLVED subtree, e.g. `key = json.dumps(OmegaConf.to_container(cfg.dataset, resolve=True), sort_keys=True)`, and add a loud guard in `Run.dataset`: `getattr(ds,'split_seed',None) == record['split_seed']` alongside the existing n_train check (the n_train check alone cannot see a data-seed swap).

findings.issue: The report's mechanism percentages cannot be reproduced from the npz cache it writes, and are attributed to the wrong k. Report: 'only 74 % of the residual is inside Sven's k=16 (89 % inside k=B=32)' and 'MNIST keeps 99.93 % -> 92.9 % in the top 64'. Recomputed from the delivered files (seed means of sum_{i<k} utr_i^2 / sum utr_i^2 at the final checkpoint): polynomial Sven k=16 -> 58.82 % (init 55.11 %), k=32 -> 73.71 %, k=105 (the rtol-kept count) -> 89.59 %; MNIST-labelreg probe512 Sven -> init 99.946 %, final 99.868 % (the 2000-row file gives 99.96 % -> 86.4 %). So '74 %' is the k=32 value and '89 %' the top-105 value, i.e. the sentence understates how much k=16 truncation discards; no natural variant (energy/||r||^2, L1, (utr/sigma)^2, trajectory mean, online batch utr/resid_norm) reproduces 74/89/92.9. Phase B / the paper would quote these.
findings.suggested_fix: Recompute the residual-fraction numbers from `load_spectra` with the k taken from the record (toy 32, poly 16, MNIST 64) and restate them with the k they belong to; toy's '100.0000 % in the top 32' and 'rtol 0.03 keeps 12 -> 105 of 673' (recomputed 12.4 -> 104.6) are correct as written.

findings.issue: `verify_checkpoint(run, step=S)` loads the model at step S but compares it against the LAST recorded value: `epoch` stays None, so `run.recorded(which, epoch=None)` returns `curve[-1]`. Measured on toy Sven mseed1000: `verify_checkpoint(run, step=64, detail=True)` returns recorded=1.643e-07 (= val_final), recomputed=1.208, rel_error=7.35e+06, with no error or warning. The `step=` path is accepted by the signature, documented only as 'the state at the end of epoch', and is not exercised by any test.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reject `step` unless it is an epoch-end step, or map it to its epoch label (`run.epochs[run.steps.index(step)]`) and index the curve with that; add a test.

findings.issue: `compute_one` calls `ct.verify_checkpoint(run, detail=True)` unguarded, so a run whose curve has no complete epoch kills the whole CLI invocation AFTER its spectra have been computed (the work is discarded and the remaining runs never run). Reproduced: `tools/compute_ckpt_spectra.py polynomial_scan --methods LBFGS --seeds 2000 --probe 8` -> uncaught `ValueError: ... no epoch has both a checkpoint and a recorded 'val' value`. The diverged runs are precisely the L-BFGS/KFAC ones a phase-B `--methods all` pass would include, and the report presents this case as handled.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the verify in try/except, store `verify_rel_error = nan` plus the reason in the npz, and keep going (the spectra themselves are computable by step).

findings.issue: `resolved_config`'s safety net compares `OmegaConf.to_yaml(cfg.get('dataset'|'model'))` WITHOUT resolving, so it is blind to exactly the fields the campaign parameterises by interpolation: two configs that differ only in `data_seed`, `n_data` or `mlp_width` render identical dataset/model subtrees (`seed: ${data_seed}`, `n_train: ${n_data}`, `hidden_dims: [${mlp_width}...]`) and never trigger the documented 'disagreement RAISES rather than picking one'. The candidate filter on `result_id_fields` happens to cover these today, so the guarantee advertised in the docstring rests on the filter, not on the check.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `OmegaConf.to_container(cfg.get(key), resolve=True)` (with the parent attached) instead of the raw YAML, so an interpolated difference is seen.

findings.issue: `checkpoint_spectra` takes `spec = run.row_spec`, i.e. the PER-RUN RowSpec, and `row_spec_for_scan` (which exists for exactly this) is never called by the tool or the CLI. Baseline records carry no `kappa`, so comparability with the Sven run holds only because `RowSpec.from_record` defaults to kappa=2 and the three diag Sven runs happen to use kappa=2.0 (verified). On a scan whose Sven ran kappa!=2 the baselines would silently get different rows while the module docstring promises 'the same rows Sven differentiates'; `mnist_kappaScan_labelRegression` holds kappa 1/2/3, and `row_spec_for_scan` there returns whichever svd_ run sorts first (kappa=2) with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Let `checkpoint_spectra`/the CLI take an explicit `spec=` defaulting to `row_spec_for_scan(scan)`, and make `row_spec_for_scan` raise (or warn) when the scan's svd_ records disagree on kappa/signed_residual.

findings.issue: Two verification claims in the report overstate what the numbers show. (a) 'Cross-check vs the spectra SvenGram logged online ... max rel diff over SVs above 1e-6 sigma_max = 1.0e-08...3.3e-07 (steps 0-781, all three scans); at late toy steps it grows to 2e-4'. Recomputed for toy Sven mseed1000 from the reloaded checkpoint + reconstructed batch, with that same 1e-6 threshold: 2.36e-04 at step 0, 4.12e-04 at step 1, 2.23e-04 at step 2, 4.36e-05 at step 4, 1.21e-03 at step 64 - it is already ~1e-4 at the FIRST step; only the SVs above 0.1*sigma_max agree to 3-5e-08 (and the online array is float32, so ~1e-7 is the floor anyway). (b) 'abs error <= 2.2e-8 everywhere' is contradicted by the same bullet's own CIFAR numbers: my independent recompute of CIFAR-labelreg Sven mseed4000 gives rel 2.447e-05 (matching the claimed 2.4e-05) but abs 1.214e-05, and nanoGPT rel 2.2e-08 on a 1.73 loss is abs ~3.8e-08.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate (a) as 'the leading singular values agree to ~5e-08; below ~1e-2 sigma_max the float32 Gram loses precision (up to ~1e-3 relative even at step 0)' and (b) as 'abs error <= 2.2e-8 on the MLP/LM scans, <= 1.3e-5 on the BatchNorm CIFAR scans'.

findings.issue: `param_vector`'s state_dict branch with `names=None` selects every floating tensor, which for a ResNet includes the BatchNorm `running_mean`/`running_var` buffers - the docstring says 'Buffers are left out ... so the norm and the distance from initialisation are over the trained weights only'. Delivered numbers are unaffected (`distance_from_init` and `checkpoint_spectra` always pass `names` from the model), and the unit test uses a buffer-free MLP, so nothing catches it.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the state_dict branch to the module's parameter names (or document the branch honestly) and add a BN-module case to the test.

findings.issue: `checkpoint_spectra` sets `theta0 = None` (and writes `dist_init = NaN`) when the run's own file has no step 0, while `distance_from_init` falls back to the record's `ckpt_init_file` for exactly that case. A `final`-policy run (every non-diag scan) therefore silently yields an all-NaN `dist_init` column.

Doc nits. (a) The CLI's cost guide ('~28 s per run' toy/poly, '~45 s' MNIST-512, '~11 min' MNIST-2000) is above what the cache itself records in `elapsed_s`: toy 20.5 s mean (max 28.7), polynomial 20.8 s, MNIST-512 27.0 s (max 31.4), MNIST-2000 467 s = 7.8 min (max 8.1) - the same inflated numbers are repeated in the report. (b) `ckpt_tools.load_spectra`'s docstring says 'newest name first' but it returns `sorted(root.glob('*.npz'))`, i.e. ascending name order. (c) With `n_probe > n_train` the file is still named `..._probe<N>.npz` although it holds the whole (smaller) pool - relevant for the varying-n_data overparam scans.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the measured times, fix the ordering sentence, and name the file by the number of rows actually used.
